body:
- Agenda doc

      - Dan: Is there an Agenda for this meeting?
      - Ryan: there is one in the invite, but it was empty
      - Dan: we should use a doc for notes and the next Agenda
  - Guava is now shaded in iceberg-bundled-guava. Please let us know if you hit problems.
  - Update the build from gradle-consistent-versions

      - Ryan: We currently use gradle-consistent-versions. That’s great in some ways, but doesn’t allow us to have multiple versions of the same dependency in different modules, which blocks adding a Spark 3 module to master. It is also blocking the MR/Hive work because Hive uses a different Guava version. Even though we shade to avoid the conflict, the plugin can only support 1 version.
      - Ryan: I’ve gone through options and the best option looks like the Nebula plugins (maintained by Netflix). There is a PR open to move to these, [#1067](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/1067). Please have a look at the PR and comment!
      - Ratandeep: What are the drawbacks of the one built into gradle?
      - Ryan: It doesn’t use versions.props, so changes are larger; use is awkward because locking is a side-effect of other tasks; much newer and requires bumping to a new major version of gradle. And, I can ask the Nebula team for support if we use those modules.
  - Bloom filters for GDPR use cases

      - Miao: For GDPR data requests, we need to scan tables for specific IDs. Even batching the requests together to minimize the number of scans, this is very expensive for large tables. Matching records are usually stored in just a few files, so keeping bloom filters for ID columns reduces cost significantly.
      - Ryan: Why doesn’t using partitioning help? We normally recommend bucketing or sorting by ID columns.
      - Miao: ID columns change between user schemas and requests may use a secondary ID not used in the table layout.
      - Owen: Why do this at the table level, if bloom filters are already supported in ORC and Parquet? Doesn’t that duplicate work?
      - Miao: We didn’t want to be tied to a specific format.
      - Owen: Are bloom filters the right solution? It’s easy to misconfigure them
      - Ryan: I agree they are easy to do incorrectly, but I think there is a good argument for this as a secondary index that is independent of the file format. Bloom filters are hard to get right, especially if you’re trying to do it while minimizing memory consumption for a columnar file format. Usually, parameters are chosen up front and might be wrong. At a table level, this could be moved offline, so indexes are maintained by a service that can do a better job choosing the right tuning parameters for each file bloom filter.
      - Ryan: I think we should think of this as a secondary index. We might have other techniques for secondary indexes, this one happens to use a bloom filter. We’ve had other people interested in secondary indexes, so maybe this is a good opportunity to add a way to track and maintain them.
      - Miao agreed to write up their use case and approach to start the discussion on secondary indexes.
  - Update on row-level deletes

      - Ryan: If you want to get involved, we’ve updated the Milestone with tasks. Tasks like writing a row filter using a set of equality values should be good candidates because they can be written independently and tested in isolation before the other work is done.
      - Ryan: Another area that could use help is updating tests for sequence numbers. We’re running all of the operations tests that extend TableTestBase on both v1 and v2 tables. I’ve added a way to make assertions for v1 and v2, using V1Assert.assertEquals or V2Assert.assertEquals so we can go back and add assertions to all of the existing tests that exercise lots of different cases. It would be great to have more help adding those sequence number assertions!
      - Ryan: In the last few weeks, we’ve added content types to metadata that tracks whether files contain deletes or data in the metadata tree. There’s currently an open PR, [#1064](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/1064), that adds DeleteFile and extends readers and writers to work with them. We decided last sync to store either delete files or data files in a manifest, but not both. Using separate interfaces enforces this in Java. I’m also working on a branch that separates the manifests in a snapshot into delete manifests and data manifests, which will help us identify everything that needs to be updated to support delete manifests.
      - Ryan: If you’d like to help review, please speak up and we’ll tag yo

body:
- Highlights

      - Parquet now supports name mapping (thanks Junjie)

          - Why it matters: this aligns more closely than the ordinal-based fallback approach to import existing data files. This should be the default for imported tables.
      - Vectorization for flat schemas was committed (thanks Samarth)

          - Why it matters: 2-3x performance improvement for flat projections, and some operations are faster than Spark, like projecting dictionary-encoded string columns.
      - An action to compact data files was added (thanks Saisai)

          - Why it matters: This extends the common library of actions to maintain or clean up a table without interfering with current readers and writers.
      - ORC metrics and predicate pushdown were added (thanks Edgar and Shardul)

          - Why it matters: These will bring ORC performance more in line with Parquet because ORC will be able to skip files using metadata, and row groups using pushdown.
  - Upstream ORC fixes may require an 0.8.1 release

      - Owen will help monitor when it is time and can be RM for the patch release
  - 0.9.0 release planning

      - Ryan: now that Spark 3 has been released, we should get Iceberg support for it released with an 0.9.0. What else do we want to target for that release?
      - No other features were suggested, will target just Spark 3 support
  - Spark 3 progress and roadmap

      - Ryan: Split the Spark module into 3: the original iceberg-spark with common classes, spark2 for classes that implement the 2.4 DSv2 API, and spark3 for classes that implement the 3.0 DSv2 API.
      - Ryan: There is some risk because the iceberg-spark classes build against 2.4 and reference the public API, as well as InternalRow. Any issues should be addressed by thorough testing ahead of time.
  - Row-level deletes

      - Ryan: Since last sync, we’ve committed the updates to track DeleteFile instances in metadata, along with an operation to add them, RowDelta. We have not exposed methods to remove delete files, instead we have updated various operations to clean them up (e.g., dropping a partition drops its delete files). This includes pruning delete files that are older (by seq number) than all data files.
      - Next steps:

          - Job planning: Add delete files required on read to FileScanTask, update planning to perform the 2-phase approach.
          - Delete encoding: Add reader/writer for delete files and filters to apply deletes while reading.
      - Junjie: is there an update on the Spark metadata column PR? It hasn’t been updated recently.

          - Ryan: This was not going into 3.0 so I didn’t follow up yet. I can update it.
      - Junjie: has the design doc diverged from the implementation?

          - Ryan: No, the implementation is really similar to what we originally planned.
          - Junjie: Yes, but many details have been decided that aren’t in the doc.
          - Ryan: Good point, I’ll update the spec soon with a PR to improve docs.
      - Deleting rows added in the same commit ([problem write-up](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/issues/360#issuecomment-645207673)) / equality delete files

          - In the CDC use case, if a key is added twice during a checkpoint, we need a way to handle this. One suggestion is to use a dynamic delete encoding, where every row could have a different set of equality columns.
          - Owen: Why would you need to delete a row twice instead of just writing it once?
          - Ryan: The use case is when you’re writing a stream of CDC events. The writer should not need to buffer events to dedup until an entire file is written out. So the writer will write and forget about events as they arrive.
          - Ryan: I think the idea using dynamic columns is to remember the last row and delete it specifically, using more columns than just the key. For example, a CDC event timestamp would work.
          - Ryan: But there are problems with that approach.

              - If such a CDC event is duplicated, both would be deleted by the “expanded” equality delete. And if there is no unique value in the row (no event timestamp) it would be even easier.
              - This makes encoding much harder, requiring a complex map schema for values. This is slower to read and slower to apply as a filter.
          - Ryan: The alternative I had been planning to build is allowing positional deletes to apply to data files with the same sequence number. That way, if a writer needs to delete an earlier record, it just needs to know the position where it was written in the current data file. That’s a more targeted delete without the duplicate issue, and doesn’t require keeping as much state -- just the key and a position, rather than the key and any other identifying data (e.g., timestamp or all data columns).
          - Owen: sounds good.
          - Ryan: I’ll reply on the issue and include this in the summary.
  - Gautam: how are others monitoring dataset health?

      - Discussing [additional metrics](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/issues/617) about datasets, like number of manifests, number of data files, etc.
      - Ryan: What is the use case?
      - Guatam: We want to know when tables are misconfigured or need attention. For example, when commits take too long due to retries, or when scan planning takes a long time. Are current stats enough?
      - Ryan: That would be useful, we don’t currently do much to keep track of those. I think the current approach of emitting events to listeners is good, but we will need to add more data to those events, like how long a commit or planning run took. We can also start tracking total number of metadata files in snapshot summaries to emit with the events for context.
      - Edgar: Should we add similar listeners to the catalogs?
      - Ryan: That’s a good idea, so you could know how long it took to create or drop a table.

      - Here is the Hive issue for adding something like this to Hive itself: <https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HIVE-12679>
      - This looks like something similar in Hudi - <https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HUDI-306>

body:
- 0.9.0 release status

      - Upstream ORC release

          - Not a blocker
      - Spark 3 integration is nearly ready
      - Anything else for the release?

          - Guatam: working on additional metrics in scan events and snapshot summaries (non-blocking)
  - Hive InputFormat progress

      - Serde is committed, InputFormat is next. What is the IF status?

          - Adrien (from AirBnB) will post a branch based on the mapreduce IF
          - Ryan: IF should be a drop-in replacement, so it doesn’t matter which one we use, correct?
          - Edgar will get an ETA for the PR and we can use the Expedia one to unblock the next steps if it isn’t going to be soon.
      - After IF, next steps are StorageHandler and more tests, then predicate pushdown, column pruning, and metadata tables
      - Adrian (from Expedia): PPD is simple, just need to adapt it to the IF
      - Found bug when MR job is launched in distributed mode, @guilload and @rdsr are taking a look at it and will propose a fix soon (see #1243)
      - Waiting PR for predicate pushdown from @cmathiesen and @massdosage
      - Adrian and Christine will give a talk at Subsurface conference on 30 July
  - Row-based delete progress

      - Not much progress since focus is on the 0.9.0 release
  - Filip: will pick up the change-detection API for schema update

      - Use case: upstream service that makes sure the schema is correct before the data hits Iceberg. Currently works with Spark schemas, which are observed schemas. This use case requires column addition and type promotion.
      - Ryan: Sounds like this is a schema union use case, if you can’t change the incoming data schema.
      - Should this also support promotion to optional from required? Maybe, with a configuration option.
  - Miao: Should the indexing proposal cover full indexing or file skipping?

      - Guatam: what about row group skipping?
      - Ryan: the model we’ve used so far is to delegate responsibility for skipping within a file to the file format, and use table-level metadata to skip whole files. This is to keep table-level metadata to a manageable size. So probably scope this to file skipping.

  - Hive integration

      - Shaded Jar - agreed to follow example of iceberg-spark-runtime, i.e. new Gradle subproject to produce the jar, to be called iceberg-mr-runtime or iceberg-hive-runtime. Will include all dependencies except Hive itself, shaded and relocated as appropriate to not clash with Hive’s classpath.

  - ORC support

      - NameMapping is committed, working on metrics for import and metrics config
      - When is the new version expected? Would be nice to get some bugs fixed

          - Edgar: the timestamp bugs
          - Ryan: will this be problematic to integrate if we don’t have a reliable version?
          - Shardul: we relocate ORC, should be reasonable to rely on a specific version
  - Parquet column index implementation

      - Parquet 1.11.1 update
      - Xinli: looking at Iceberg code to integration page-level filtering, should have a PR soon because it doesn’t look too hard
      - Ryan: will also need to sync up rows in pages, in addition to filtering

  - Row-level delete update

      - Major milestone: all customers are enabled, all new datasets are in Iceberg

body:
- Highlights

      - Flink writes for DataStreams and SQL are committed (thanks OpenInx)
      - SortOrder was added (thanks Anton Okolnychyi)
      - Python create table support (thanks Ryan Murray)
  - 0.10.0 release planning

      - Need to release Hive read support and Flink write support in the next few weeks
      - Ryan: what else should be in the release?
      - JDK 11 job planning bug

          - This is a release blocker, probably related to ParallelIterator
          - Jacques: we’ve seen issues with spliterators when moving from 8 to 11. The issue is Spliterator from an iterator with a size, Java 8 will ignore it but Java 11 passes it
          - Ryan will open an issue and link to failures [Update: found the problem and opened a [PR](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/1446) to fix it instead.]
      - Should we wait to release until Hive read projection is committed?

          - Probably not, considering the issues that [Adrien raised](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/1417#issuecomment-686830961)
      - Junjie: Can we add Spark Structured Streaming read support? ([PR #796](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/796))

          - Ryan: last time I looked, I didn’t think it was ready and the time to iterate on this PR is long (review -> update -> review round trip time). I’d personally rather not gate a review on adding big features when others would be delayed, but I’ll spend time to review so that if it is ready we can get it in.
          - Jacques: How do we want to decide on cases like this?
          - Ryan: I think we usually try to release when needed to get features out to people that have contributed them. That’s important, and I’d like to handle situations like this by having another release for the feature that might instead cause a delay. (Note that this happened with Flink write support in 0.9.0 as well)
      - Junjie: Flink has a bug where Java serialization IDs do not match between a new job and checkpoint state if Iceberg is upgraded

          - Junjie will open an issue for this bug [Update: [Issue #1438](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/issues/1438).]
          - This affects jobs that are recovering from a checkpoint or savepoint and have an updated Iceberg version because serial version IDs are not set
          - Ryan: It’s been a long time since I’ve thought about how to serialize across versions with Java Serializable
          - Jacques: Isn’t the best practice to not use Java serialization across versions?
          - Ryan: I agree, we should consider other options instead
          - Ryan: Is this a release blocker? Probably
  - Partition functions

      - Time zone parameterization ([PR #1368](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/1368))

          - Ryan: A user reported issues with daily partitioning because day boundaries in partitions do not align with the expected day in the user’s time zone. In general, we don’t want partition boundary points to matter to users, but there is an issue here because data can’t necessarily be deleted up on the expected boundary. Deleting data is one case where the partition boundaries do leak. One fix is to use hourly partitions, but that may not be appropriate for some use cases. Another solution is to add an offset parameter to the date/time transforms to allow adjusting boundaries. I wanted to discuss that option with a larger group.
          - Jacques: You would need to support time zones
          - Ryan: What if we used just an offset (+/-HH:MM) to avoid needing a time zone map that needs to be maintained and updated?
          - Jacques: Then the boundaries would be wrong during DST
          - Owen: Agrees that zones would need to be supported
          - Russell: This would only get uglier
          - Jacques: What about custom hidden partitioning? That would allow users to maintain these themselves rather than adding them to Iceberg
          - Ryan: That is a good idea. We’ve considered it a bit and I think we can support functions with two main cases: monotonic functions, like date/time transforms, and everything else, like bucket. (Not including identity, of course.) This is probably a better solution to the problem.
          - Ryan: This use case also seems like a temporary problem. Row-level deletes could be used in the future to avoid this problem.
      - How to handle between bug

          - Ryan: Presto found an issue where date/time transforms are off by 1 for values before the epoch, caused by using “between”. For example, there are 0 months between January 1970 and epoch (correct) *and* between December 1969 and epoch (wrong). Two options to fix:

              - Fix the Java implementation, but adjust projected filters for scans to match data written to the wrong partitions. This would result in scanning an extra partition for all scans with data older than the epoch.
              - Update the spec to match the Java implementation and deprecate the existing date/time transforms with the problem. This is okay because it is unlikely that there are other implementations.
          - Jacques: quiet +1 for option 2
          - Russell: that would lead to 2 implementations with different behaviors
          - Ryan: the new transforms could be more clear, using names like utc_date_ordinal
          - Someone: Would this be exposed to users or would it not be as confusing as having multiple functions
          - Ryan: that’s correct: existing tables would continue to use the current functions, but the API would create partition specs with the fixed functions. It would be nearly transparent to users. Only implementations would need to care.
          - Owen: Sounds reasonable
          - Russell: Sounds good
  - File formats

      - Jacques: we are thining about CSV and JSON integration
      - Owen: ORC release candidate with stats bugs fixed should be released soon
      - Edgar: PR for ORC name mapping when importing data needs review ([PR #1399](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/1399))
  - Linear timestamps?

      - Ryan: There is a discussion on the mailing list about trying to make timestamps monotonically increasing for a table to make it easier for incremental consumption. There is an open PR to add Clock to TableOperations, which would be the “right” way to do this. That would allow injecting a clock that is synchronized across nodes using a central time source.
      - Jacques: Jamming this into snapshot timestamp seems hard. Even with a common time source, commits could still be out of order.
      - Ryan: Yes, this is why we came up with a different way to do versioning within table metadata for delete files. If you have a strategy to wait until after the last commit’s timestamp (even using a central time oracle), a bad timestamp could also prevent commits for an unknown amount of time.
      - Owen: User transaction IDs could be useful
      - Ryan: There is already a way to inject IDs to track external commits in Iceberg metadata. We use this for exactly-once semantics in Flink.
      - Ashish: What happens if you have multiple jobs with the same ID?
      - Ryan: I think we commit in parallel and then cherry pick only one commit with a given ID.
  - Row-level delete update

      - Current outstanding work:

          - Update Spark to apply delete files while reading [Update: [PR #1444](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/1444)]
          - Update MR (and maybe Flink) reads to apply delete files, or to fail if delete files are in a task
          - Add validations for various operations. Position deletes should validate that data files with new deleted records are still present in the table
          - Now that the design has been implemented in the Java “reference implementation”, we need to document it and update the spec.
      - Ashish: How are out of order events handled?
      - Ryan: Through the validations. Operations will need to validate the assumptions that they make when committing. We still need to build these and the validations are dependent on the operation. For example, UPSERT using position delete should validate that data files are still present (not rewritten), but UPSERT using equality deletes does not need additional validation.
      - Ryan:
  - [Distributed Job Planning](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/issues/1422)

      - Russell: Opened PRs for two options to parallelize job planning for large tables.

          - Update ManifestGroup to be able to delegate to a distributed engine implementation
          - Rewrite ManifestGroup internals using Spark
      - Ryan: We will take a look
  - Handling missing files in metadata tables

      - Russell: Concurrent runs of RemoveOrphanFilesAction and ExpireSnapshotsAction caused the expiration to fail: remove orphan files deleted files that were no longer referenced by the table, but expire snapshots was scanning the previous metadata tree. Should tables based on metadata locations ignore missing files?
      - Ryan: That’s only safe to do this for the set of files that used to be reachable because we want to remove those. Skipping missing files in the current metadata could result in deleting data files that are in currently valid snapshots (although possibly not accessible due to missing metadata files). Probably best to avoid this by coordinating when the actions run. Removing orphan files can be done much less often and should not be done concurrently with expiration.
      - Russell: makes sense.
title: Iceberg Community Sync notes, 2020-09-09

body:
- Highlights

      - Flink reads for DataStreams and SQL are committed (thanks Jingsong Lee)
      - ORC imports now use NameMapping (thanks Edgar Rodriguez)
      - Docs for Spark streaming, table maintenance, Hive, Flink (thanks Jungtaek Lim, Adrian Woodhead, and OpenInx)
  - 0.10.0 release planning

      - What remaining bugs should be fixed?

          - Tagged under 0.10.0 release milestone
          - Mention a committer on github to have more bugs added
      - Any blockers for new big items?

          - Anton: [REFRESH behavior](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/issues/1485) for Spark with caching disabled should be fixed. A fairly simple fix is working locally already [[#1545](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/1545) was committed]
          - Anton: Had a problem with RemoveOrphanFiles action where extra paths were deleted. Need a fix for path matching, possibly ignore some of the URI components (scheme, authority) and add a threshold to fail over-deleting.

              - Russell: a threshold sounds concerning. There are lots of cases where more files could be (correctly) deleted than the table contains
              - Jacques: Why not make this a 2-step process: generate files to delete and then delete them?
              - Russell: We could optionally return a DataFrame like we added to the ExpireSnapshots action.
              - Anton: We should get a fix to avoid incorrectly deleting files for the release, improving debugging is also a good step but separate
          - Ryan: Read paths either need to apply delete files or fail if delete files are found in a v2 table and are not supported. Need updates to MR and Flink [MR updated in [#1497](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/1497), Flink updated in [#1517](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/1517)]
      - [SQL expression compatibility?](https://lists.apache.org/thread.html/r1f02485a6c007715939f9ee9aa33344b8cfc90e5f72fa68e5d989056%40%3Cdev.iceberg.apache.org%3E)

          - Shardul: need to fix ORC pushdown, that is the only correctness issue because Spark will filter out any additional records. [[#1536](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/1536) was committed]
          - Will target 0.11.0 for the SQL-compatible factory methods, like Expressions.sqlNotEqual
  - [SQL extensions](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/1473)

      - Anton: Apple has implemented copy-on-write delete and update and plans to contribute. First step is to get the stored procedures in, which adds Iceberg SQL syntax extensions and rules. Draft PR is available, will be merged in smaller PRs after 0.10.0.
  - [Migrate/Snapshot Actions](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/1525)

      - Russell: Action API for SQL extensions to migrate from session catalog to Iceberg tables
  - [Distributed Job Planning](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/issues/1422)

      - Russell: Discussion concluded that we should use a Spark-specific path for distributed planning in Spark. One of the blockers is getting PartitionSpecID In Metadata tables.
  - Row-level delete

      - Ryan: Someone asked about two-phase planning status. Status is that it is implemented in master and will be available in 0.10.0. This is what the DeleteFileIndex does.
      - Compactions (Minor / Major) - Edgar: Has a use case where they want to minimize the number of delete files. Minor compactions to compact delete files and major to rewrite data files without deletes. Are any of these available?

          - Ryan: Delete file compaction is not available yet, but the data compaction action that exists should correctly apply delete files.
          - Anton: would like to contribute the actions
          - Edgar: will take a look, check on whether other options work
          - Anton: could adapt copy-on-write behavior to this
          - Ryan: would a normal rewrite work?
          - Anton: no, INSERT OVERWRITE doesn’t have the same guarantees. Would need to have a way to turn on validation that no new data is added.
  - Hive integration

      - Column projection: still waiting on a fix, but probably won’t make it into 0.10.0
      - Hive metadata hooks are making progress, may be done by 0.10.0
      - Documentation - minimal for 0.10.0 or wait longer for more?

          - Minimal is a good start, enables adding more slowly in multiple PRs
  - [Localized data storage](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZluOiRZlmsfNnQJLSqTiBQg7-XeSE-gvEOn2e0y6E54/edit#heading=h.cuifpdpzmfqz)

      - Mick: Looking at using a LocationProvider to distribute data into geographically distributed buckets for compliance requirements. Compute can be centralized and the logical dataset is identical, with changes transparent to users. Anyone else have this problem or is interested in the LocationProvider?
      - Kyle: When storage is separated by country, do you not need to process the data there?
      - Mick: Local data, central compute is the most relaxed option. Working on validating this, but think there are use cases for it.
      - Jacques: What about stats in metadata?
      - Mick: Metadata is still centralized
      - Ryan: Stats can be configured at a column level and can truncate. It may be possible to turn off stats for sensitive columns like identifiers, or truncate to a length that avoids the problem.
  - Didn’t get to topics:

      - Docker examples with notebook
      - Iceberg-aws module
      - Secondary indexing
title: Iceberg Community Sync notes, 2020-09-30

body:
- Highlights

      - Congratulations to new committers Jingsong Lee and OpenInx!
      - Flink and MR read paths apply row-level deletes (thanks Junjie!)
      - Hive supports 3.x and can create and drop tables (thanks Marton Bod and Peter Vary!)
  - 0.10.0 release

      - Expected timeline

          - Based on the outstanding items, aiming for a candidate in 1 week, on 28 October
      - What remaining bugs should be fixed?

          - Anton: Remove orphan files problem
          - IN predicates are slow with too many items

              - Russel: can we avoid pushdown from Spark?
              - Ryan: I think we should only disable when evaluation is expensive
              - Anton: Disabling pushdown from Spark will prevent evaluation for partition pruning, which does not have the problem
      - Any blockers for new big items?

          - Flink manifest file serialization
      - Gio: what about getting the Glue catalog in?

          - Ryan: we’ve been preparing to release 0.10.0 for a while and we try not to hold a release for specific features. We prefer to make another release when the features are ready instead.
          - Anton: other features are also waiting, like stored procedures in Spark
          - Gio: it would be nice to get this out before re:invent
          - Ryan: that should be possible. We can release 0.11.0 next month

<!-- end list -->

  - AWS Glue Catalog

      - Jack: the initial PR was too much code; updated it to use the Glue API directly, and will add a separate PR for dynamo-based locking. Also working on dynamic FileIO loading.
      - Jacques: How do the Dynamo and Glue integration tests work?
      - Jack: tested against AWS, but integration tests are ignored in the PR
      - Jacques: Can we build a github action that works around the credentials problem so we don’t need to ignore tests? Secrets can be kept and decrypted by actions
      - Gio: will take a look at getting credentials and getting integration tests to run
      - Ryan: side note, we may want to move to github actions for this?
      - Jacques: github actions are better, but it is harder to test some things and you can have different actions for different branches
  - Nessie catalog

      - Jacques: have been working on a Nessie Iceberg catalog for several months, but integration testing was a blocker until a local server was available. Gradle plugin was the easiest path and should be in the PR in the next few days
      - Jacques: 2 questions for the group

        1.  Like git, everything is a commit in Nessie. Do we want a commit message and a standard way to store it?

              - Ryan: we already have snapshot summary metadata, which is where I would put a commit message. Then we just need to decide on a well-known key. But, how would you specify a commit? There’s no good way to do this in SQL, for example, like there is for a git commit (bring up an editor, continue after save).
        2.  Should we create a cross-table transaction concept in Iceberg?

              - Jacques: The pattern we want is where many operations to different tables can be done in a single commit. That would change the refresh model (currently single table) where refreshing one table would also refresh others involved in the commit, and would require a way to commit in a single operation.
              - Jacques: Should we sketch out how that would work?
              - Ryan: Yes, that sounds valuable.
              - Anton: We have use cases for this where we currently use write-audit-publish, but it is not ACID compliant.
              - Ryan: We use the same pattern, but cherry-picking commits like this requires no other writers. A lot of the challenges are easier if the full state of the commit is preserved, rather than trying to recover it when moving changes on to the current table version.
  - Dynamic catalog loading

      - Ryan: Since we are adding Glue and Nessie and possibly JDBC catalogs, should we make catalog loading dynamic like recent proposals for LocationProvider and FileIO?
      - Jack: Just posted a PR for this
  - Format V2

      - Ryan: it is a good time to talk about v2 changes because we want to release the format with row-level delete support, but we also don’t want another breaking change soon. So we want to finish all of the known format changes for v2.
      - Ryan: we’re currently tracking this under a v2 milestone. If you have any other tasks, please open an issue and we’ll add it to the v2 milestone.
      - Current tasks & goals:

        1.  NaN tracking
        2.  Row-level deletes
        3.  Partition spec field IDs
        4.  Snapshot schema tracking
      - Gio: Yan is working on NaN tracking for Parquet and then ORC
      - Anton: should we also include DISTRIBUTE BY in a table definition?

        1.  Ryan: good question, I’m not sure. Jacques, what do you think?
        2.  Jacques: not sure whether this fundamentally equivalent to partitioning, will think about it
  - Row level Delete progress

      - Validations are committed
      - Ready for 0.10.0 release
  - Spark engine support for UPSERTs

      - Ashish: looking for UPSERT support in Spark, what is the status?
      - Anton: Currently blocked on SQL extensions, which will go in after the 0.10.0 release. After Iceberg can extend SQL, we will add MERGE INTO and other commands. Initially copy-on-write, which should be easy to adapt to merge-on-read. Long-term goal is to move the implementations to Spark.
      - Ryan: merge-on-read implementation also depends on finalizing v2

<!-- end list -->

  - Page skipping PR

      - Xinli: the PR is working great, but has a corner case if the whole row group is skipped by the column index. There is a discussion on how to fix upstream in Parquet, and there may be a work-around for Iceberg.
      - Ryan: when would this happen? Iceberg will do the stats filtering
      - Xinli: stats are coarser at the column level in the footer, so column stats don’t rule out a match, but page-level stats do like a hole in the middle of stats. The case is rare. Will probably fix by adding how many values are skipped, then the update is easy.
title: Iceberg Community Sync notes, 2020-10-21

body:
- Highlights

      - 0.10.0 release is almost passing (Thanks Anton!)
      - Dynamic FileIO and Catalog extensions (Thanks Jack!)
      - S3FileIO added (Thanks Dan!)
      - SQL extensions are committed (Thanks Anton!)
  - Parquet page skipping

      - Xinli: Parquet filter limitations led to wanting to reimplement filters in Iceberg. While this has worked for row group filtering, page-level filtering would require Parquet-specific classes in Iceberg, like the column chunk reader. ColumnChunkPageReadStore is not public.
      - Ryan: For context, we ran into a lot of issues when trying to use filters built into Parquet. One of the main problems was implementing id-based name resolution. Parquet’s implementation considers a column missing to be all nulls, but does the “missing” check based on column name. So filters need to be rewritten for each data file’s schema. Getting the schema requires an extra footer read. We concluded that fixing this problem would probably require a major change to Parquet APIs that was not really possible at the time. We also wanted to use Iceberg expressions.
      - Julien: Using your own expression makes sense, but it is probably best to delegate most things to Parquet, like page reading and decoders.
      - Ryan: Is it worth considering the benefit of having an Iceberg-specific PageReadStore? Iceberg has different IO APIs and we could implement vectored IO more easily with one.
      - Julien: We should avoid exposing too big of an interface to the world from Parquet
      - Jacques: it doesn’t make sense why there is so much Parquet-specific code in Iceberg
      - Dan: We can move some things upstream, like Arrow readers
      - Ryan: The intent was always to move as much as we can upstream when it makes sense to do it. Maybe now is a good time to introduce that Parquet v2 API and move some of this. Let’s talk about it in the Parquet community.
  - Secondary indexes

      - Miao: An internal milestone has been taking time, but planning to resume work on secondary indexes. The missing part is the read path. For the write path, there is a high level design doc that is ready to review. Already building bloom filter indexes and that PR is ready to merge internally. The design doc has performance results.
      - Ryan: What do you need from the community?
      - Miao: Help on the read path and feedback.
      - Jacques, Anton: Would need to pass option to Spark context, not sure how.
      - Russell: Read option bug was fixed in Spark 3.1. Non-catalog read path can’t pass read options in 3.0.
      - Miao: Will update after internal review.
      - Ryan was going to link to the issue for this in these notes, but there is no open issue.
  - S3FileIO features

      - Dan: The current S3FileIO implementation is basic. Uses typical GET and PUT operations. We’re planning to move to S3FileIO from our FS implementation and can add features in Iceberg where people are interested:

          - Vectored IO: We have an implementation with vectoried IO: passing in a series of offsets and buffers. (This is much better for S3 because it can use bounded GET requests to avoid pulling more data than needed.) The question is where the interface should live.
          - Multi-part and progressive uploads: PUT imposes a file size limit, so will need to support multi-part upload. By progressively uploading parts as the file is written, this can also avoid bursty network behavior. ([PR #1767](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/1767))
          - Remote request signing: replacing the signer in the S3 client allows moving request signing to a service that performs authorization checks. Other cloud providers may also support something similar.
      - Jacques: Dremio has internally iterated on the read path (vectored). The API is narrow, using CompleteableFuture and is async. Can contribute implementations for Azure and S3, working on one for Google. Works by decorating FileSystem with additional interfaces and has scatter/gather without too much coupling.
      - Ryan: Where should all of this live? Parquet, ORC, and Iceberg need access to call these APIs. It doesn’t make sense for them to live in any one project.
      - Julien: People complain that Parquet depends on Hadoop, would be nice to have an abstraction for this to avoid that dependency. SeekableInputStream is all that’s needed.
      - Dan: vectored IO makes this more difficult
      - Ryan: upstream of all of these projects seems right in the long term. Right now, Parquet and Iceberg have nearly identical interfaces and Iceberg has classes to adapt from Iceberg to Parquet.
      - Julien: That isn’t horrible currently.
      - Jacques: Memory management becomes an issue. Arrow has the potential to be the foundational upstream project. Since we use Arrow elsewhere, we could put the interfaces there. (Arrow does have FS interfaces, just not in Java)
      - Ryan: Sounds like we should start a conversation across communities to find out where this should live.
      - Dan: Jack, is your multi-part upload progressive?
      - Jack: No, it uses transfer manager. Let’s open an issue for further discussion [linked above]. Also have KMS / server-side encryption ready.
  - DELETE FROM and MERGE INTO

      - Anton: DELETE is still in a bit of a rough state and is ideally part of Spark in the long term, but it is currently passing tests and supports a good number of query cases. Will write a doc and submit to Spark, but it will take time.
      - Ryan: I just want to highlight this work as a step toward merge-on-read using v2: DELETE FROM support is the first step, then MERGE INTO. After the copy-on-write implementations are in, then it will be fairly straightforward to adapt them for merge-on-read.
      - Anton: We are running these internally and are confident in the design and implementation. Getting this into Iceberg is largely driven by community interest.
  - Hive progress

      - Peter:

          - Starting to take on Hive reads using Iceberg as storage. Expedia provided the read path, but there are some problems that are getting fixed as test coverage improves.
          - Also working on basic writes. There is a working solution for unpartitioned (and maybe partitioned) tables. Unit tests are passing, but probably has edge cases. Will push it forward like the read path by testing more and fixing problems as they are identified.
          - Waiting for 0.10.0 to go out, then we can work on merging the others.
      - Ryan: Could we break up writes to get this in more easily? It’s much easier to review smaller PRs.
      - Peter: First priority is to create tables with normal column definitions and fix timestamp problems. Not sure how to break writes down further, but will think about it.
  - V2 work

      - Ryan: I’ve been thinking about the question from last sync about whether we need to get DISTRIBUTE BY done by v2. I don’t think we do. The reason why we wanted to get sort order in is that v2 has requirements for not dropping sort order if it is going to be used in row-level deletes (for streaming merge of equality deletes). There is no similar requirement for DISTRIBUTE BY, so we can add it if and when we need it.
      - Anton: Anyone looking into adding sort id to individual data file metadata? That’s the last step for v2 and ordering. (Also: anyone looking at optimizing how delete files are read? Multiple uses will open multiple times in the current implementation.)
      - Yan: will look into sorting.
  - Praveen: Relative paths in table metadata?

      - Not much time for this discussion. Continued on [Issue #1617](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/issues/1617).
title: Iceberg Community Sync notes, 2020-11-11

body:
- Highlights

      - Several stored procedures are available (Thanks Anton!)
      - Glue and Nessie catalogs were added (Thanks Jack and Ryan!)
      - Hive:

          - Create DDL supports schemas (Thanks Peter!)
          - Projection pushdown works (Thanks everyone!)
  - Release 0.11.0

      - What needs to be done?

          - Runtime Jars for new catalogs

              - Ryan: The main thing is that we need to make it easy to use the new catalogs. Now that we can plug in catalog implementations, there is no need to package everything into the runtime Jars, making them even bigger.
              - Jacques: Would it make sense to have a threshold or size budget for inclusion in runtime Jars? There is also cost to maintain runtime Jars and user friction to add them in an environment
              - Ryan: I really like the idea of an inclusion budget. One additional reason not to include these is the required updates to LICENSE and NOTICE, although that would be required for individual runtime Jars anyway.
              - Jack: AWS may create a runtime Jar
              - Ryan: What would the threshold be? If it is 1MB, then we could fit a lot in. Also, we had a bad Parquet version that increased the size by 15MB and hardly anyone noticed. While it’s good to keep this low, maybe we don’t need to worry too much. That about doubled the size.
              - Russell: Current size is 17MB
              - Jacques: Nessie is very careful to not pull in much to make it light-weight. Hoping to get into the existing runtime Jars.
              - Ryan: Maybe this should be case by case or we shouldn’t worry about it much. I have no problem adding small catalogs, let’s decide separately.
          - DELETE FROM will be ready, may be able to get MERGE INTO done

              - Later: possibly won’t get this done since we’re aiming for a release in 2 weeks
          - Hive config updates

              - Would be nice to get Hive configuration changes decided and implemented for 0.11.0
          - OpenInx (not present) also suggested targeting Flink CDC writer, streaming reader, and rewrite actions.
      - What is the target date?

          - Given that the holidays are approaching, this probably needs to be done in 2 weeks or would be pushed until January. Consensus was to aim for the next 2 weeks.
          - Ryan: May not be able to get MERGE INTO done in that case
          - Ashish: Will share a [working PR](https://github.com/aokolnychyi/incubator-iceberg/pull/3/files) and will work with Anton to get this in
  - External file-level data

      - Partition sketches
      - Secondary indexes
      - Ryan: we have two proposals that seem similar to me because they are proposing large metadata blobs. It is also likely that these would be updated asynchronously and would need to keep track of how current the metadata is. I’d like to see if we can use the same storage mechanism for both.
      - Jacques: How do people feel about querying the same version and having things happen differently? These should influence performance, not behavior.
      - Ryan: I agree, these are performance optimizations. I’m okay with different performance, and it would not be a dramatic change. Asynchronous updates would mean that the majority of the metadata is up to date, but the latest data may not be indexed yet.
      - Jacques: Would the table metadata change for these?
      - Ryan: Yes, I think that any index data should be committed and tracked by the table format so that engines can share it. This would be a metadata update.
      - Owen: How would you manage updates of sketches if it isn’t in table metadata?
      - Miao: In draft, file pointer is in metadata using a relative path. Will send the draft proposal to the dev list tonight. The read path is difficult because this needs to hook into job planning.
      - Ryan: We could have a way to plug in a filter that is passed the file pointer for file-level metadata. This is a little more difficult because there is a trade-off for planning time vs task execution time. Planning should generally not open a file per split, but it may make sense in some circumstances. [Later thought: this would work well with the DELETE FROM approach, where all files are first scanned for matching deletes, then a second job actually does the rewrite.]
      - Jacques: Are there multiple scopes? Sketches would be partition level, but indexes would be file level.
      - Ryan: Yes, good point.
  - Relative file paths

      - Ryan: We’ve had several suggestions to support relative file paths. We’ve so far avoided this because it is simpler for a location to be canonical. For example, in RemoveOrphanFiles and ExpireSnapshots actions we rely on equality checks to determine whether a file is still referenced by a table. Relative paths or transformations of paths makes this harder to maintain.
      - Miao: Use case is migrating storage. Currently rewrite locations, which is not ideal.
      - Owen: Use case is managing multiple stores by using a virtual path scheme. Another use case is replicating tables across clusters.
      - Ryan: I’ve suggested an approach where a custom FileIO is used to translate existing paths. Opening an hdfs path could match rules that redirect that to another store.
      - Owen?: The problem is that works like magic.
      - Ryan: You’re right. And FileIO would not be used for comparison, so that problem still exists for expire snapshots and remove orphan files. In that case, my FileIO suggestion is probably a bad idea.
      - Ryan: Then what would this look like? Some people have suggested paths relative to other metadata files, which I don’t think would be a good idea because it would be so complex. Would this be limited to a relative path from the table location?
      - Jacques: Could we make actions to rewrite locations based on the existing code? Seems useful.
      - Ryan: Yes, that would be good because a relative location doesn’t solve the problem entirely. You’d need to rewrite to change the base table location. [Does this mean that it is unsafe to alter table locations?]
      - Praveen: What are the next steps?
      - Ryan: I think we should write up a design doc detailing how it would work. Will a mix of fully-qualified and relative paths be supported? How do we address the expire snapshots problem?
  - Row-level operations in Spark

      - Built the support for “Merge Into” internally on top of Anton’s work on Delete, looking forward to collaborating on future pending items. [Early PR](https://github.com/aokolnychyi/incubator-iceberg/pull/3/files)
      - OpenInx is working on writer interfaces
      - DELETE FROM is almost in
  - Not enough time:

      - Multi-table transactions

          - [PR #1849](https://github.com/apache/iceberg/pull/1849) adds TransactionCatalog
  - Next sync: 6 January because of holidays. See everyone next year!
title: Iceberg Community Sync notes, 2020-12-02
